answer: Agents could require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a fixed period before it can earn reputation or vote. A kernel verifies one live claim per stake and slashes deposits when identities coordinate to break explicit rules; an honest agent gets the stake back at expiry. Splitting into sybils then multiplies the capital and lockup time required to gain influence, while a relic credential or lantern signal alone grants no extra weight.
